title: An open and closed map with connected target and one finite fibre has at most that many connected components

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a connected component of a topological space, and the fact that a space with at least N components decomposes as a disjoint union of N nonempty open and closed pieces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on connected components, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the decomposition that the proof applies to the source of the map.

core_obligations: Induction on the number of components: if the source has at least N connected components the proof produces a decomposition of the source into N nonempty open and closed pieces (proof lines 993-995).

Push forward along the map: since the map is both open and closed, the images of those pieces are again open and closed, and connectedness of the target forces each of them to be the whole target (proof lines 995-998).

Count the fibre: every piece therefore meets the chosen fibre, so the fibre has at least N elements, which is the contrapositive of the asserted bound on the number of components (proof lines 998-999).

The consequences: the author's closing sentences about components of the source being open and closed and mapping onto the target follow from the bound together with the same open-and-closed argument (statement lines 987-989, concluded at proof line 999).
proof_roadmap: 反设源至少有 N 个连通分量，把源分解为 N 个非空开闭子集之不交并。
由 f 既开又闭，各像仍开闭；Y 连通迫使每个像等于 Y，于是所取纤维至少含 N 个点，得矛盾（即分量数上界的逆否）。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the bound on the number of connected components of the source of an open and closed map with connected target and one finite fibre (author lemma at source lines 980-990, label lemma-finite-fibre-connected-components), including the consequences that the components are open and closed and map onto the target. The proof (source lines 992-1000) is a compactness-free counting argument: a decomposition of the source into N open and closed pieces is pushed forward, connectedness of the target collapses each image to the whole target, and the chosen finite fibre then has at least N points (proof lines 993-999). H2.
